_comment: Visual-review verdicts per domain (worst→best: critical/flaw/clean, plus 'blocked' for domains with no capture to review — hard 403 / bot wall), kept separate from auto-scored *--score.json so re-running the sweep never overwrites them. The gallery merges these and can sort by verdict. Notes describe the CURRENT state only (no fix history). Update after eyeballing a re-captured clip/cast. PROVENANCE: `by` is 'ai' for a model-written verdict and 'human' for one a person confirmed; absent means UNKNOWN (bulk-entered before this field existed — treat as unverified). This file previously described itself as human-reviewed, which was not true: AI review has produced confident, specific notes that did not match the image (walmart's empty section headings and ytmusic-album's missing title were both filed as 'clean'). An existing verdict is NOT evidence a person looked. SCOPE: a verdict judges the CAPTURE, never the site's willingness to serve us. A bot-gate stub, hard 403 or challenge page is 'blocked' — nothing reached the pipeline, so it measures the wall, not the clipper (homedepot was filed 'critical' for exactly this). A PAYWALL that withholds the body is likewise not a capture fault: the clip faithfully shows what the page served, so it is 'clean' (wired, nature, asahi, economist) — downgrade only for what the CLIPPER then does wrong, e.g. globeandmail filling the missing body with promo rails. READ ENOUGH BANDS: slice-clip.py defaults to 3 because content buried under prepended chrome does not reach band 1, and a verdict asserting absence from one band cannot tell MISSING from BURIED (both apnews verdicts claimed the article was replaced by a video rail; it was present from band 3).
